input.quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
input.rationale: Compliant at (in fact above) the preferred position. Section 10(a) is a genuine Vendor-side obligation to "indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer" against all third-party Claims, including reasonable attorneys' fees. Its limbs are subject-matter triggers rather than cause-of-action triggers: "(i) the Services;" "(ii) the Auction Platform;" (iii) Creative placed onto Customer's platforms or websites by the Auction Platform; "(iv) Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement or (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Kubient control with respect to Kubient's obligations hereunder." Any third-party allegation that the Services, Auction Platform or delivered Creative infringe or misappropriate IP is a Claim "arising out of or in connection with" limbs (i)-(iii), and Vendor misconduct (including gross negligence/wilful misconduct and breaches of law that breach its warranties) falls within (iv)-(v). The deterministic check for "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" fails only as a phrasing artefact — the clause never uses the words "infringe" or "intellectual property" — but the substantive scope required by the rule is met, so this is not a rule failure. The indemnity is also stronger than the fallback: there are no Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund sole-remedy limitation, and no 3x super-cap; Section 7(a) expressly carves indemnification liability out of the consequential-damages waiver. Section 11 supplies the preferred procedural element (prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay, indemnifying-party control of defence and settlement, no liability-admitting settlement without the indemnified party's consent, cooperation at the indemnitor's cost). Two sub-preferred points are noted for leverage only, not redlined: our reciprocal indemnity in Section 10(b) is broader than "Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law" (it also reaches unauthorised use, breach of warranty and Customer acts/omissions), and the Creative limb is qualified by "to the best of its knowledge." Per the playbook's classification semantics these are minor shortfalls of the preferred wording, and the clause as a whole benefits us, so no redline is proposed.
